headline: Sharks’ Adam Gaudette to make season debut against Bruins
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Sharks forward Adam Gaudette will make his season debut against the Bruins. He missed the first four games with an upper-body injury and was a healthy scratch for the seven games after that.

Gaudette steps into a San Jose team whose results are running ahead of its play. The Sharks are 6-4-1 with 13 points, but they have created only 44% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season, and 45% at five-on-five. Their goalies have helped a lot: goals saved above expected, which compares the goals a team allows to what the shot quality would predict, is +8.1 for SJS. The power play is a modest bright spot at 0.69 expected goals per game, while the penalty kill allows 0.94. Boston is 8-2-1 and also leans on goaltending, at +12.7 saved above expected, with a 53% five-on-five share. The Bruins' overall share of 49.8% is nearly even, so this is a tougher matchup for the Sharks than the record suggests. Gaudette's return gives San Jose another option, but the gap in underlying play is what matters here.
